halt_handoff.text:
Loop 10 ended at HALT_LOOP_CAP - I made 10 loops, the configured maximum, and the backlog still has items I didn't reach. This loop ran the Critic phase only (Step 1): per SKILL.md's own routing table, reaching loop_cap forces state HALT_LOOP_CAP, and that state skips Step 2 (Architect) and Step 3 (Execution) - so no code changed this loop. Everything below is a fresh, independently re-derived review of current source (build green, 138/138 tests green, no diff from loop 9), not a rehash of loop 9's numbers.

The most important thing this loop found: a genuinely NEW, unfixed Serious-severity bug (Finding F-014), discovered by tracing a doc comment's safety claim through its actual mechanics rather than trusting it. IsLibraryOperationBlocking() (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:191-201) is checked by every per-game button (Restore Backup, Edit artwork, Search artwork) before they start their own async work, but none of them ever claims the flag - so a header button (Refresh/Fix Library/Restore Changes/Revert Defaults) can start and replace the entire game list while a per-game operation's own file I/O is still in flight, and when that operation resumes it silently writes its stale result onto the freshly-reloaded entries instead. This is the same class of bug as F-001 and F-005 through F-009 (all already fixed, all Serious deduction), found in the same file after 9 prior loops of dedicated session-guard sweeps missed it - because every prior sweep checked only the per-game-session direction (a second click superseding the first), never the per-game-vs-bulk-operation direction. It is fully actionable (no network-call behavior involved, so the STANDING USER CONSTRAINT does not block it) and is Priority 1 for whenever this run resumes.

Separately, and exactly as the run's own standing instruction anticipated: Finding F-011 (LoadGameEntriesAsync's sequential per-game network calls, PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:455-679) remains open and remains genuinely blocked - not by lack of loop budget, but by the STANDING USER CONSTRAINT (no behavioural oracle for changes to per-game network-call ordering/concurrency against SteamGridDB/GOG/Epic/Ubisoft) plus a real prerequisite (StoreNameLookup's three caches, FixLog's three static fields, and SteamGridDbClient.CapsuleParseNotes are all unlocked, safe today only because nothing calls them concurrently). A decision from you - whether observable network-call ordering/concurrency is allowed to change here - is the one thing that would unblock it; nothing else this run can do will.

Progress so far (loop 1 -> loop 10, all in REVIEW_HISTORY.json): architecture_quality 8.0->7.5 (a DOWN at loop 5, held since), state_management 6.5->7.0, domain_modeling 8.5->9.5, data_flow 7.5->7.5 (dipped to 7.0 loops 6-8, recovered loop 9), framework_idioms 8.0->9.5 (peaked at 10.0 loops 8-9; this loop's own G6 re-check found a fresh residual - see Finding-adjacent Scorecard note - and moved it back to 9.5), concurrency 6.5->6.5, simplicity 7.0->8.0, test_strategy 6.5->6.5, credibility 7.5->9.5. Scorecard average moved from 7.33 (loop 1) to 7.94 (loop 10). Nine findings landed and independently re-verified holding (F-001, F-002, F-003, F-005 through F-010); one new Serious finding (F-014) surfaced this final loop, unfixed.

Never moved: test_strategy (10 loops - the only dimension whose numeric value has never changed even once since loop 1; the blocker is a genuine platform constraint, PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs binds to Windows.UI.Xaml which has no desktop test projection, not an unaddressed choice), architecture_quality (10 loops since its last UP, though it did drop once at loop 5), concurrency (3 loops since its last UP), state_management (3 loops since its last UP).

Current Priority 1 (carried forward):
  - F-014: single-game artwork operations check IsLibraryOperationBlocking only at the click, never claim it, so a bulk operation can start and corrupt freshly-loaded entries mid-flight - Serious deduction, fully actionable, not blocked by the STANDING USER CONSTRAINT.
  - F-013 (Priority 2): the same three-way UI-thread entry-update duplication carried since loop 9, with this loop's own correction: the previously-claimed 'observed drift' in RestoreAllChangesAsync is not a bug (it correctly never touches the backup flag, since ArtworkFiles.ReapplyCustomisationAsync never touches the backup file) - the duplication itself is still real, the drift framing was not.
  - F-011 (Priority 3, blocked): sequential per-game network calls in LoadGameEntriesAsync - blocked by the STANDING USER CONSTRAINT, see above.

Next step options:
  (a) Bump cap and resume - "/contest-refactor --cap 15" continues from here; F-014 is ready to be the next loop's Step 2/3 target with no further investigation needed.
  (b) Accept current state - 10 loops landed 9 verified fixes and the codebase is materially more trustworthy than at loop 1, but F-014 is a real, live, Serious-severity bug left unfixed; accepting means shipping with it present.
  (c) Answer the STANDING USER CONSTRAINT question for F-011 - tell me whether changing per-game network-call ordering/concurrency against SteamGridDB/GOG/Epic/Ubisoft is acceptable, and a resumed run can act on F-011 too.
  (d) Reset - "/contest-refactor --reset".

findings.title: Single-game artwork operations check IsLibraryOperationBlocking only at the click, never claim it, so a bulk operation can start and corrupt freshly-loaded entries mid-flight
findings.why_it_matters: A user can click Restore Backup (or pick artwork from the grid/search panel) on one row, then click Refresh, Fix Library, Restore Changes or Revert Defaults before the first click's file I/O completes; the second operation replaces the whole game list with newly-built objects, and when the first operation resumes it silently writes its now-stale result onto the freshly-loaded entries for that image instead.
findings.what_is_wrong: IsLibraryOperationBlocking (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:191-201) is checked by RestoreBackup_Click (:1859), EditGameImage_Click (:1233) and SearchGameImage_Click (:1637) before starting their own single-game async flow, but none of those flows ever sets isLibraryOperationRunning, so the check only guards against a bulk operation that is already running at click time. TryBeginLibraryOperation (:207-220), used by RefreshButton_Click (:725) and ConfirmAndRunAsync (:787, the shared guard behind FixLibraryButton_Click/RestoreChangesButton_Click/RevertDefaultsButton_Click), checks the same single flag with no awareness of an in-flight single-game operation, so it succeeds and lets LoadGameEntriesAsync clear and rebuild GameEntries (:359, :699) with brand-new GameEntry instances while, for example, RestoreBackupCoreAsync's own await (ArtworkFiles.RestoreOriginalAsync, reached from :1907) is still pending. When that await resumes, EntriesSharingImage(game) (:328-330) searches the now-replaced GameEntries for entries matching the stale captured game's image path and writes Image/ImageFileName/HasBackup onto whatever it finds - the freshly-loaded entries, not the ones the user's click was about.
evidence: SteamGridDB.Xbox/PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:191-201 (IsLibraryOperationBlocking - check only, never claims the flag)
findings.leverage_impact: None - this is a missing claim on an existing gate, not a Module boundary.
findings.locality_impact: Fully contained inside PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs; the fix mirrors the exact idiom already used to close F-005 through F-009.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Reachable from ordinary UI interaction with no special timing skill required (click one per-game button, then click any header button before the first finishes), and it silently corrupts user-visible tile state (image, filename, or the backup flag that controls whether the Restore Backup button even shows) with no error surfaced - the same class of harm F-005 through F-009 were rated Serious deduction for, discovered in the same file after 9 prior loops of dedicated session-guard sweeps missed it because every prior sweep traced only the per-game-session direction (a second per-game click superseding the first), never the per-game-operation-vs-bulk-operation direction.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Give IsLibraryOperationBlocking's callers the same claim/release discipline TryBeginLibraryOperation already provides bulk operations, sized for a single-game operation: set isLibraryOperationRunning (or a dedicated single-game counter) before the await and clear it in a finally in RestoreBackupCoreAsync, ReplaceImageCoreAsync and the grid/search picker's download-and-apply path, so TryBeginLibraryOperation/ConfirmAndRunAsync cannot start a bulk operation while one is in flight - matching the mutual exclusion IsLibraryOperationBlocking's own doc comment already claims but the check-only implementation does not deliver.

findings.title: ReplaceImageCoreAsync, RestoreAllChangesAsync and RestoreBackupCoreAsync duplicate the same UI-thread entry-update loop three times
findings.why_it_matters: Any future change to what happens when a game's tile image is replaced (a new derived property, a new visual state, a new field to keep in sync) has to be found and added by hand in up to three places, and the three copies already differ in which fields they set with no shared explanation of why - a future edit that does not understand RestoreAllChangesAsync's own semantics (it reapplies a saved customisation without touching the backup file, so HasBackup correctly stays untouched) could easily blur that distinction by copying one of the other two blocks.
findings.what_is_wrong: ReplaceImageCoreAsync (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:1154-1192), RestoreAllChangesAsync's per-entry block (:1067-1135) and RestoreBackupCoreAsync (:1900-1950) each independently dispatch to the UI thread via OnUiThreadAsync and foreach over EntriesSharingImage(game), writing entry.Image and entry.ImageFileName in all three, entry.HasBackup in two of three (RestoreAllChangesAsync omits it - correctly, since ArtworkFiles.ReapplyCustomisationAsync never touches the .bak file the flag reflects, but nothing in the shared shape documents that distinction), and StatusText.Text conditionally in two of three.
findings.leverage_impact: Three call sites drop to naming their own image/backup-flag values instead of re-deriving the whole dispatch-and-foreach shape.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Same leaf-module-duplication class as Finding F-002 and F-003 (both resolved), in the same file - a third, smaller instance that survived nine loops of scrutiny, including two dedicated leaf-module-duplication sweeps, because those sweeps focused on dialog/animation ceremony rather than this smaller entry-update pattern. The duplication's real cost is forward-looking rather than a present bug (corrected this loop - see Simplification Check): three near-identical bodies with silently different field lists are exactly the shape a future edit gets subtly wrong.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Extract a private helper (e.g. UpdateEntriesSharingImage(GameEntry game, BitmapImage image, string imageFileName, bool? hasBackup)) that owns the OnUiThreadAsync dispatch and the EntriesSharingImage(game) foreach, writing Image/ImageFileName always and HasBackup only when a value is supplied (null from RestoreAllChangesAsync, since it never changes); each call site keeps its own status-text/counter logic outside the helper, since that differs meaningfully between an aggregate bulk-operation count and a single-game message.

findings.title: LoadGameEntriesAsync resolves each unmatched game's name and SteamGridDB match sequentially, one network round trip at a time, on every widget open
findings.why_it_matters: A user whose library has many GOG/Epic games without a direct SteamGridDB match pays the full network latency of the GOG, Epic (or Ubisoft/community-database) endpoint plus the SteamGridDB name-search endpoint for every one of those games, one after another, before the library list finishes loading - which happens on every widget open, not once.
findings.what_is_wrong: LoadGameEntriesAsync's per-entry loop (PrimaryWidget.xaml.cs:455-679) awaits, in strict sequence for each manifest entry: sgdbClient.GetGameByPlatformIdAsync (:581), then when unmatched one of StoreNameLookup.GetOrFetchGogNameAsync (:603) / GetOrFetchEpicNameAsync (:612) / GetUbisoftGameNameAsync (:621), then StoreNameLookup.FindGameByNameAsync (:641) - each entry's network calls fully complete before the next entry's loop iteration starts any of its own. The awaits are independent across entries; this is a sequential-independent-effects shape (efficiency lens D2).

builder_notes.pattern: A guard's own doc comment claiming a protection is not evidence the protection actually holds in both directions - trace the implementation's mechanics, not the comment's claim.
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A method name or doc comment says 'blocks X while Y is happening' but the implementation is a one-directional check (read a flag, branch) rather than a two-directional claim (set the flag for your own duration too). Ask: does every OTHER path that could conflict also respect this same flag, including paths that start AFTER this one and finish BEFORE it?
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: For any 'IsXBlocking()'-shaped guard, find every caller that CHECKS it and confirm at least one of them also SETS the flag the check reads, for exactly the duration the check is trying to protect - a check-only caller is trusting someone else's claim, not making its own.

builder_notes.pattern: A prior loop's characterization of a 'bug' or 'drift' needs its own evidence chain re-walked, not just its file:line citation trusted, before being carried forward unchanged - the callee's actual contract can make an apparent inconsistency correct.
